name: Underbelly Whelp Scale
summary: South of Lake Everstill, Underbelly Whelp Scale trades hands among Redridge craftsmen. Black dragon whelps provide the pliable scales, and local artisans value them when coin is scarce.

sections.title: A Rare Trade Commodity
sections.body: Black dragons bear tough scales, but facing a full-grown one is deadly for ordinary folk. South of Lake Everstill, black dragon whelps nest among the crags. Their back plates can be brittle or coarse, while the softer scales beneath their bellies bend more readily and still offer protection. Those qualities make Underbelly Whelp Scale valuable in local trade. Craftsmen prize it, and creditors can accept it in place of coin.

sections.title: Verner's Debt
sections.body: In Lakeshire, craftsmen sometimes barter when coin runs short or trade routes are strained. Verner Osgood, the local blacksmith, owes a heavy debt to Argus, a blacksmith in Goldshire. The debt began with a shipment of shoes brought in from Goldshire. Argus favors rare trade goods, so Verner depends on travelers to gather underbelly whelp scales. They can help settle what he owes and keep his workshop in good standing.

faq.q: Where do Underbelly Whelp Scales come from?
faq.answer: Black dragon whelps provide Underbelly Whelp Scale. They roost in rocky cliffs and hills south of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains, and the scales can also be gathered from mature whelps such as Snarlflare.

faq.q: Why does Verner Osgood want these scales?
faq.answer: Verner Osgood owes Argus, the blacksmith in Goldshire, for a shipment of imported horseshoes. Argus accepts dragon scales as payment, and any extra scales give Verner material for making tough protective gear.

faq.q: Why are underbelly scales preferred over regular dragon scales?
faq.answer: Young dragons' underbelly scales are pliable enough to cut, shape, and sew into practical armor or reinforced gear. Their dorsal scales are often too rigid, thick, or warped for ordinary leatherworking and smithing techniques.

faq.q: Why are black dragon whelps in Redridge at all?
aliases: why are there dragons in redridge
faq.answer: The Black Dragonflight has kept a presence in the burning peaks and crags along the borders of the Burning Steppes and Redridge. Its whelps brood and grow in the high, hard-to-reach cliffs.

angles.text: Argus and other artisans value these scales for their strength. They can be worked into linings, grips, and specialized protective fittings, stronger than ordinary cowhide.

As an Alliance traveler, you know Lakeshire's isolated defenders depend on barter with Elwynn Forest to stay equipped. Dangerous local bounties such as dragon scales help maintain the town's supplies.
